definition.en-US: Running a program on a computer you control, such as your own computer or a rented server, instead of using a website that someone else runs for you.

analogy.en-US: Like cooking dinner at home instead of ordering takeout, so you choose the ingredients and you clean up afterwards.

definition.en-US: Software whose source code is published so that people can read it, and whose license says how they may use and change it.

analogy.en-US: Like a recipe card that anyone can read, copy and adjust, as long as they follow the terms written on the card.

definition.en-US: A program that keeps organised records, such as accounts and resumes, so that other programs can save, search and change them.

analogy.en-US: Like a filing cabinet with labelled folders, where every record has its place and can be found again.

definition.en-US: A setting that connects a port number on your computer to a port number inside a container, written as host:container.

analogy.en-US: Like the sign at a building's front desk that sends each visitor to the right room number inside.

definition.en-US: A regular test that a container runs to report whether its program is ready and working.

analogy.en-US: Like a traffic light that shows whether a road is open, without moving any cars.

definition.en-US: A private value, such as a password or a signing key, that an app needs and that must not be shared.

analogy.en-US: Like the spare key to your house, which opens the door for anyone who holds it.

definition.en-US: A file in a project folder that lists the files and folders Git should not record when you make a commit.

analogy.en-US: Like a note on a shared fridge that tells everyone which items to leave alone.

definition.en-US: A copy of data kept somewhere else, so that the data can be recovered after a mistake, a failure or a bad update.

analogy.en-US: Like a spare set of house keys kept at a neighbour's, so you can still get in if you lose yours.

definition.en-US: A script that changes the layout of a database so that a new version of an app can read and write it.

analogy.en-US: Like moving the papers in a filing cabinet into new folders when the office adopts a new labelling system.

definition.en-US: The legal terms that say what you may do with a piece of software, such as use, copy or change it.

analogy.en-US: Like the rules on a library card that say what you may borrow and for how long.

definition.en-US: A written record of the events a program or container reports while it runs, usually with the time and a message.

analogy.en-US: Like a ship's logbook, where each entry notes what happened and when.

definition.en-US: A situation in which two programs try to use the same port number on one computer, so that one of them cannot start.

analogy.en-US: Like two people trying to sit in the same chair, so one of them has to find another seat.
